headline.purpose: Page greetings and identity lines (dashboard greeting, ticket detail student name).

body.purpose: Default dashboard content register: tickets, DARS trees, correspondence, tables.

label.purpose: Section headers, form field labels, category tags. The system's only uppercase/small-caps register.

components.name: State Dot
components.description: The single source of status truth: a filled circle in maroon/gold/ink, reused verbatim across tickets, DARS requirements, caseload, and legends.
components.css: .ds-state-dot { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background-color: #8c1d40; flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid ink call-to-action button, e.g. "Sign in as an advisor".
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #17140d; color: #fbf9f3; padding: 12px 20px; border-radius: 6px; border: none; font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(23,20,13,0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8c1d40; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Transparent ink-bordered button that inverts to solid ink on hover, e.g. landing nav "Sign in".
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #17140d; border: 1px solid #17140d; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #17140d; color: #fbf9f3; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8c1d40; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Resolve Button (signature)
components.description: Press-and-hold commit button: an 850ms fill gesture stands in for a signature before a ticket is recorded as hard-resolved.
components.css: .ds-resolve-btn { position: relative; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #17140d; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: #17140d; user-select: none; background: transparent; } .ds-resolve-fill { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #17140d; transform-origin: left; transform: scaleX(0); transition: transform 850ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1); } .ds-resolve-btn:active .ds-resolve-fill { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-resolve-label { position: relative; mix-blend-mode: difference; color: #fff; }

components.description: Caseload / summary card: raised paper on ruled ground, hover border strengthens.

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Login form field: raised paper, rule border, maroon focus border.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #fbf9f3; border: 1px solid #ddd4bd; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 12px; font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #17140d; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #8c1d40; }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Left icon-rail navigation item; active state is a solid ink pill.
components.html: Overview
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 12px; font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; text-decoration: none; color: #4a4536; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: rgba(221,212,189,0.4); color: #17140d; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #17140d; color: #fbf9f3; font-weight: 500; }

narrative.overview:
Vizor for Advisors reads as a page from a physical ledger, not a SaaS dashboard: warm paper ground, a visible 32px ruled baseline grid running under every screen, and status recorded the way a ledger records a transaction — as one of exactly three committed states, never a decorative badge. The world is a Bauhaus foundation-workshop discipline (primaries as load-bearing law, never ornament) fused onto ASU's own maroon-and-gold identity and real academic-records content: DARS requirement trees, ticket queues, session transcripts.

The system is flat by construction. There is no shadow vocabulary anywhere in the build — depth comes from tonal contrast between the ruled paper ground and opaque raised surfaces, and from 1px rule borders, never from elevation. A geometric sans (Archivo) carries navigation, numerals, labels, and the landing display headline; a companion serif (Source Serif 4) is reserved for headline-scale moments — page greetings, ticket subject names, the login prompt, and one italicized accent phrase on the landing hero — rather than for body copy generally. Dashboard body text (ticket correspondence, DARS line items, summaries) renders in the sans at a small, dense size suited to fast triage, not leisurely reading.

The three state colors — maroon, gold, ink — are rationed and never used decoratively outside status law. The same three colors and the same filled-dot mark answer the same question everywhere they appear: does this need the advisor, did the student resolve it, or did the advisor commit a resolution.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a visible, structural 32px ruled baseline grid (repeating-linear-gradient, --color-rule), painted over by opaque surfaces where they need a clean field.

Exactly three load-bearing state colors — maroon (needs the advisor), gold (student self-resolved), ink (advisor hard-resolved) — reused verbatim across tickets, DARS requirement status, and the landing legend.
Flat throughout: zero box-shadow in the shipped codebase. Depth is tonal (paper vs. paper-raised) and linear (1px rule borders), never a drop shadow.
Archivo (sans) for structure — nav, numerals, labels, the landing display headline; Source Serif 4 reserved for headline-scale prose moments, not body copy.
A permanent three-pane desktop shell: icon rail, content, and a persistent right rail carrying the state-key legend and the live caseload — not page-specific content, part of the system.

rules.name: The Rationed Three Rule
rules.body: Maroon, gold, and ink are the only colors ever assigned meaning by status. They appear in exactly one place across the whole system — StateDot's DOT_CLASS map — and every surface that shows status (ticket rows, DARS requirement trees, the caseload strip, the right-rail legend, the landing legend bands) reads from that same map. No status is ever shown as a muted gray pill or a fourth color.

rules.name: The Never-Decorative Rule
rules.body: Outside status law, maroon and gold do not appear as accent color. Buttons, links, and chrome use ink and the neutral scale only; the two state colors are reserved entirely for the moment they mean something.

rules.name: The Headline-Only Serif Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 is spent only at headline/title scale (page greetings, a ticket's student name, the login prompt, one landing accent phrase). Reading-dense dashboard content — ticket bodies, DARS trees, correspondence — stays in the sans at body size. Where the direction contract framed the serif as a reading-content face, the shipped build reserves it for headline moments instead; that's the standing rule going forward.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: No surface ever casts a shadow. A surface reads as 'raised' only by switching from paper to paper-raised and gaining a rule border — never by gaining a shadow.

dos: Do assign maroon, gold, and ink only through StateDot's shared color map — any new status surface should read from that map, not invent a new color or a gray pill.
Do keep the ruled baseline grid as the page's ground plane; new full-bleed sections should paint over it with paper-raised or a state color rather than hiding it with a container shadow.
Do reserve Source Serif 4 for headline-scale moments (greetings, names, the login prompt); keep dense dashboard content — tables, correspondence, DARS trees — in Archivo at body size.
Do use the authored 1.75-stroke icon set for structural/navigational marks; do not mix in an icon library or use icons to signal status.
donts: Don't introduce box-shadow anywhere; the system is flat by construction, with zero instances in the shipped build.

Don't use maroon or gold decoratively (accent color, hover tint, illustration) outside their status meaning — the one confirmed exception is the maroon focus ring/border, itself a 'needs attention' signal.
Don't add a fourth state color or a muted/neutral status pill; the grammar is rationed to exactly three, by design.
